title: Build sinusoidal and rotary position encodings
brief: Write the sinusoidal clock encoding, the matrix that moves it k positions, and the rotary tables that make a score depend only on the offset.
hints: Hand i turns at speed omega_i = 10000 ** (-2 * i / d). The angle at position p is p * omega_i, so np.arange(T)[:, None] * omega[None, :] gives every angle at once. Write the sines into columns 0::2 and the cosines into columns 1::2.
In offset_rotation, the block for hand i sits at rows and columns 2*i and 2*i + 1 and equals [[cos, sin], [-sin, cos]] for the angle k * omega_i.
For rope_tables, the speeds are theta ** (-2 * np.arange(d // 2) / d). Concatenate np.cos(angles) with itself along the last axis, so each speed appears in both halves and the table has shape (T, d).
rotate_half(x) is np.concatenate([-x[..., half:], x[..., :half]], axis=-1), and apply_rope returns x * cos + rotate_half(x) * sin.
rope_score builds tables with T = max(m, n) + 1 rows, rotates q with row m and k with row n, then takes the dot product.
